title: Area of a Parallelogram — Refine, Practice & Quiz
topic: Cumulative review of area strategies from Days 5-8

items.prompt: A parallelogram has a base of 9 units and a height of 7 units. What is its area?
A rectangle has an area of 96 square units and a width of 8 units. What is its length?
A parallelogram has a base of 11 units, a height of 4 units, and a slanted side of 7 units. What is its area?

misconception_key.B: used the slanted side instead of the perpendicular height (the target misconception for the representation study)
misconception_key.C: added base + height instead of multiplying
misconception_key.D: used only one dimension (base) and ignored height

items.rationale: Area = base x height = 11 x 4 = 44. This item is intentionally identical in structure to Day 8's d8_q4 (same distractor types, new numbers) so the same misconception can be tracked before/after and across representation-image conditions.

items.prompt: An L-shaped figure is enclosed by a 9-by-8 rectangle with a 3-by-2 missing corner. What is the L-shape's area?
Which shape's area formula requires identifying the perpendicular height, not the slanted side length?

choices.D: All of the above use only side lengths

items.rationale: A parallelogram's slanted side is not the same as its height, so the height must be identified separately.
